answer: New agents must post a stake that erodes like a dune: it is locked and released only as the agent completes verified work for distinct, long-lived principals. Each finished job leaves an ember — a signed receipt chained to that principal’s history — so a fresh identity starts cold and must earn warmth over weeks. A Sybil farmer faces a ridge of cost: every clone needs its own stake and its own trail of receipts, and clones vouching for each other are discounted when their receipts share the same narrow provenance. One trusted identity is cheap; a thousand is ruinous.
